title: Avoid returning to 'high-threat areas' after domestic calls: jury
subtitle: Coroner's inquest jury issues recommendations in death of Ryan Nowlan, 39, shot by RCMP officers responding to assault, threats at Kingston Peninsula house
article: A jury investigating the 2021 death of Ryan Nowlan, shot by two RCMP officers during a domestic violence call, has suggested police in the same situation avoid heading back into high-threat areas for non-vital reasons.

During the two-day coroner's inquest held by deputy chief coroner Michael Johnston at the Saint John Law Courts, 12 witnesses testified about the events of Nowlan's death on Dec. 31, 2021, with a five-person jury ruling Wednesday that his death was a homicide due to gunshot wounds to the chest and abdomen.

The jury issued six recommendations, including "avoiding, when possible, further contact" between the parties in a domestic dispute and to "avoid re-entry of potential high-threat areas to retrieve non-vital belongings."
Johnston thanked members of the Nowlan family who attended Tuesday, saying "I can only imagine how difficult this was for them." Stepmother Cathy Nowlan declined an interview request.

On Tuesday, court heard that a then-31-year-old woman and her preteen daughter had come to the Hampton RCMP detachment just before 4 a.m. after Nowlan had choked the woman and slammed her head into the door before taking her and her daughter's cellphones. She said as she started to leave, with another child left sleeping inside, Nowlan threatened to burn the house down if she went to police.
Cst. Monique Sears told the inquest she and Cst. Christian Cunningham planned to return with the woman to get her remaining child before returning the next day to handle the task of arresting Nowlan.

The woman came into the house with them over concerns it would be unlawful entry for the officers to go in alone without a warrant, Sears said. She said the woman also asked for the phones, which Sears said were necessary for the woman's safety and security.
